$comment: Every dependency advisory this project knowingly accepts. Enforced by
- any advisory NOT listed here fails the build, at any severity
- every entry needs ghsa, package, owner and reviewBy
- reviewBy in the past fails the build (the exception has expired)
- an entry whose advisory has been fixed upstream is reported so it can be deleted
pnpm 9.15 cannot express these exclusions itself: auditConfig.ignoreCves
matches on CVE ids and this advisory is GHSA-only with no CVE.
This file is the reviewable, expiring record instead of a silent --ignore flag.

exceptions.title: deepmerge mergeObject() allows prototype poisoning of returned objects
exceptions.runtimeExposure: deepmerge is reachable only through Jest's development/test configuration loader and is not imported by production entrypoints. Jest merges repository-owned static configuration, not HTTP requests, corpus records, or other attacker-controlled objects. Exploitation would require write access to the test configuration, which already permits arbitrary code execution in the developer or CI context.
exceptions.reason: deepmerge@4.3.1 is the latest npm release and has no patched successor. The latest jest-config@30.5.2 still depends on deepmerge ^4.3.1, so a Jest major upgrade would not remove the advisory. Accept the dev-only exposure temporarily rather than pinning an unreviewed source commit or suppressing the audit globally.
exceptions.exploitability: An attacker must already be able to modify repository-owned Jest configuration or another trusted input to the test runner; no production request path reaches this package.
exceptions.owner: Developer (remove on a patched deepmerge release or Jest dependency change)
exceptions.revisitWhen: a deepmerge release newer than 4.3.1 is published or Jest removes the dependency
